senses.sense_definition: A person, thing, or idea that precedes the development of something else; a predecessor or earlier form.

examples.text: Many historians consider the ancient abacus to be a direct <w>forerunner</w> of modern computers.
This early acoustic device served as an important <w>forerunner</w> to the contemporary telephone.

senses.sense_definition: A sign or symptom that indicates the future arrival or appearance of something, especially something unpleasant.

examples.text: The dark clouds gathering over the bay were a clear <w>forerunner</w> of the impending storm.
Doctors warned that frequent headaches could act as a dangerous <w>forerunner</w> to more serious health problems.

senses.sense_definition: A non-competing participant who tests or inspects a race course or circuit before the official competitors begin.

examples.text: A skilled ski <w>forerunner</w> descended the icy slope to ensure safety conditions were acceptable for the race.
The race organizers sent a <w>forerunner</w> along the track to check for unexpected obstacles.

senses.sense_definition: A person who runs ahead of others or leads at the front.

examples.text: The solitary <w>forerunner</w> sprinted well ahead of the pack, determined to keep his lead.
An appointed <w>forerunner</w> sped forward to deliver urgent news to the waiting crowd.

traits.comment: Rare in modern standard usage in the literal running sense.

senses.sense_definition: A postage stamp used in a territory before that territory began issuing its own distinct stamps.

examples.text: The collector specialized in rare <w>forerunners</w> cancelled during the colonial era.
An authentic Ottoman <w>forerunner</w> fetched an extraordinary price at the philatelic auction.
